title: KV hostfallover, thawback and predictive-prefetch experiments
content:
Purpose:

This doc captures a set of experiments and a lightweight design proposal to reduce tail latency and cost impact when the in-GPU KV cache exceeds fast memory residency and we start depending on host memory (UMA) or PCIe-backed offload. The emphasis is on an operational strategy: graceful hostfallover, selective thawback (pulling hot entries back to GPU), and a predictive prefetch policy to avoid high tail latency spikes on token-heavy sessions.

Why this is different from prior notes:
- We focus on combining workload-aware prefetch with a cheap hysteresis-based thawback gate (rather than only eviction heuristics).
- We propose a PCIe-aware QoS signal and deadline-driven prefetch windows that tie into the request scheduler.
- The experiments are designed to produce metrics (p50/p95 token latencies, PCIe BW %, host page fault rate) that map directly to routing/fallback decisions in the serving runtime.

Background / problem statement:
- For long-context chat and multi-turn prompt workloads, KV cache size grows and GPU residency becomes constrained. We currently evict least-recently-used items and, when configured, fallback to host-resident KV pages (UMA) or paging via a PCIe-backed host page store.
- Host-resident reads add variable cost (PCIe latency + host memory access), which shows up as tail latency spikes for cold token continuations and bursts.
- Existing heuristic thresholds (static fraction of GPU memory reserved for KV, static paging thresholds) are brittle across model sizes, batch shapes, and multi-tenant noise.

Goals:
1. Reduce tail token latency degradation from host reads by 40% for high-variance sessions.
2. Keep additional memory pressure and prefetch work bounded (no >10% extra per-request CPU/PCIe overhead on average).
3. Provide runtime signals to safely failover to compatible model variants or lower-QoS paths when PCIe/host bandwidth saturates.

Design overview (high level):
- Residency tiers: HOT (GPU resident), WARM (pinned host pages / prefetch candidates), COLD (paged to disk or unpinned host frames).
- Hotset detector: per-session approximate LFU window + access recency score to label entries as HOT/WARM/COLD. Simple decaying counters (exponential decay factor tuned per model) keep compute cheap.
- Thawback gate: small bounded background worker that attempts to copy WARM entries back to GPU when (a) GPU free memory > threshold and (b) predicted reduction in host reads > copy cost. Prediction uses recent host-read latency and per-entry token frequency.
- Predictive prefetch: at request boundaries (end of decode chunk), the scheduler looks ahead N tokens in user-provided prompts/beam tokens and requests low-latency prefetch of WARM entries that are likely to be accessed in the next M tokens, subject to a PCIe budget.
- PCIe/UMA QoS signal: tracking 3 rolling metrics per-host: p95 host-read latency, PCIe bandwidth avg, host page-faults/s. When any metric crosses configured thresholds we reduce prefetch aggressiveness and trigger routing fallback policies.

Operational heuristics and thresholds (initial defaults):
- Residency labeling: entry_score = alpha * recency + beta * frequency. alpha=0.7, beta=0.3, decay half-life = 30s for chat workloads. HOT if score >= 0.75, WARM if 0.3<=score<0.75, else COLD.
- Thawback eligibility: GPU_free_ratio > 0.12 (i.e., keep 12% free for device overhead) AND expected_host_read_cost_per_sec > thawback_cost_per_sec * 1.5. thawback_cost estimated as (page_copy_time * pages) + minor kernel overhead.
- Prefetch window: lookahead N=16 tokens, prefetch budget = max 8 pages per request (configurable per-customer).
- PCIe/host safety thresholds: p95_host_read_latency > 3.5ms OR PCIe_bw_util > 70% => throttle prefetch to 30% and stop thawback until metrics stabilize.
- Panic fallback: sustained p95_host_read_latency > 8ms for 10s -> route new sessions to thinner model variant (lower KV footprint) or Dedicated capacity.

Integration with scheduler and batching:
- The prefetch requests are scheduled as a low-priority work item attached to the decode completion path. They execute against a shared PCIe bandwidth budget token system so competing requests share bandwidth fairly.
- Thawback is a background worker that acquires a small per-gpu-mutex to copy pages; copy concurrency limited to avoid burst saturation.
- When batching multiple sessions into a single step, aggregate predicted prefetch sets and dedupe page copies. This reduces PCIe work and aligns well with our kernel copy APIs.

Metrics (what to measure in experiments):
- Request-level: per-token latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), tokens served from GPU vs host vs cache-miss, number of thawbacks triggered, pages copied, prefetch success rate (prefetched entries that were used within window).
- Host-level: PCIe bw utilization, p95 host-read latency, host page fault rate, CPU worker utilization.
- Business: additional cost per 1M tokens (PCIe transfer charges + CPU time), sessions routed to fallback.

Experiment plan (incremental):
1) Telemetry baseline (2 weeks): enable fine-grained counters to establish current host-read latency distributions and per-session hotset characteristics. Collect per-model, per-batch-shape stats.
2) Conservative thawback: enable resident tagging and thawback with very small concurrency and high thresholds (GPU_free_ratio > 0.25). Run on canary hosts. Measure tail reduction and extra copies.
3) Predictive prefetch A/B: on 10% traffic, enable predictive prefetch with small budget (4 pages/request). Compare tail latencies and PCIe utilization.
4) PCIe QoS gating: enable QoS thresholds and test induced backoff under synthetic noise (background PCIe stress). Verify fallbacks trigger and are safe.
5) Ramp policy tuning: adjust alpha/beta decay windows and prefetch window size for different model sizes (7B, 13B, 70B) and workload shapes.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Over-aggressive thawback causing PCIe saturation: mitigated by throttle token bucket and immediate revert when p95_host_read_latency increases.
- Hotset misclassification for rare long-tail tokens: keep a small LRU shadow cache for extremely recent entries and fallback to synchronous host read for misses (bounded latency).
- Multi-tenant interference: per-tenant PCIe budgets, and cluster-level admission controller to avoid sharing a saturated host.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- How to account for NUMA node locality on multi-socket hosts (UMA implies different latencies depending on socket). Proposal: expand QoS signal to per-numa metrics and prefer prefetch/thawback to pages on local NUMA when possible.
- Exact decay half-lives per workload class — need more telemetry to set defaults.
- How to reconcile with kernel-level host-paging (hostpage swap) when running on air-gapped Private deployments.

Implementation notes / pointers:
- Use existing kernel copy path (serving-runtime/page-copy) to implement thawback with zero-copy where supported. Add metrics hooks before/after copy.
- Small state machine per-session for predicted prefetch sets; keep it compact (max 128 entries).
- Reuse serving runtime’s per-route QoS tokens for PCIe budgets.

Immediate TODOs:
- [Aisha] Add instrumentation PR to expose per-entry access counters and host-read timing (GH: redwood/serving-runtime#2147).
- [Marco] Prototype thawback worker that respects GPU_free_ratio threshold. (owner: Marco Ruiz)
- [Jenna] Synthetic PCIe stress bench to exercise QoS gates. (owner: Jenna Lee)
- [Ravi] Map NUMA layout on canary hosts and add per-numa counters.

References and related docs:
- See linked artifacts for GH/JIRA pointers. Also related: kv-memory-tiering-experiments and host-paging-hysteresis notes (older docs) — use them for baseline numbers but we are intentionally trying a different approach (predictive prefetch + thawback hysteresis) instead of purely eviction-first strategies.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally an experiments-first doc. Please focus review on whether the metrics and safety gates are sufficient and whether proposed thresholds are reasonable for our operational SLAs.
- If you have customer workloads that are long-context generative (>=8k tokens), add a short note about their token shape in the GH PR linked above.

End.
